cross_product_finding: Same two-tier access model as CREATE BUCKET (see createbucket.json). Notably, DROP BUCKET is also irreversible and cascades destruction of all indexes/metadata in the bucket ('Dropping a bucket deletes all data in the bucket, including documents, scopes, and collections. It also deletes all associated indexes, metadata, and other bucket resources.'), yet the gating check is still purely the Capella management-plane role, not any data-plane privilege like a hypothetical 'drop bucket' RBAC privilege - server/'s nearest equivalent (bucket deletion via REST/UI) is likewise not an RBAC-privilege-gated SQL++ operation, so this isn't a divergence from server/ so much as confirmation that bucket lifecycle management sits entirely outside the RBAC privilege model in both products - only the identity system that gates it differs (Capella org/project role vs. server/ cluster-admin credential).
